      "status": "repair",
      "strategy": "direct",
      "proposed_proof": "**Given:** A finite ensemble of states, projectors obeying the displayed bounds, and independent random codewords.

[F1] [[def-qc-density-operator]]: each $\sigma_x$ is nonnegative with trace one.

[F2] [[lem-it-finite-gentle-measurement]]: acceptance at least $1-u$ implies trace-norm disturbance at most $2\sqrt u$.

[F3] [[lem-it-hayashi-nagaoka-finite-operator-inequality]]: if $0\preceq S\preceq I$ and $T\succeq0$, then $I-(S+T)^{-1/2}S(S+T)^{-1/2}\preceq2(I-S)+4T$, with the inverse on support.

[F4] [[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]] and [[thm-non-negative-square-root-exists-and-is-unique]]: positive operators have spectral square roots and inverse square roots on their supports.

[F5] [[thm-qc-trace-norm-duality-and-norm-properties]]: for an effect $E$, $|\operatorname{tr}(EX)|\le\|X\|_1$ when $X$ is Hermitian.

[F6] [[lem-qa-30-positive-product-trace-nonnegative]]: the trace of a product of two nonnegative operators is nonnegative.

[F7] [[thm-trace-of-ab-equals-trace-of-ba]]: trace is cyclic for compatible finite-dimensional factors.

[F8] [[prop-trace-is-linear]]: trace is linear over finite sums and scalar multiples.





1.1 For a realized codebook, set $\Gamma_m=\Pi\Pi_{X_m}\Pi$ and $S=\sum_m\Gamma_m$. Since each factor is a projection, $0\preceq\Gamma_m\preceq I$. Define $\Lambda_m=S^{-1/2}\Gamma_mS^{-1/2}$ on $\operatorname{supp}S$ and zero on its kernel; add $\Lambda_0=I-\sum_m\Lambda_m$. By [F4], all $\Lambda_m$ are nonnegative and $\sum_m\Lambda_m$ is the support projection of $S$, so $(\Lambda_0,\Lambda_1,\ldots,\Lambda_M)$ is a POVM. [F4, given, construct, algebra]

1.2 For $j\ne m$, independence of $X_j$ and $X_m$ gives $$\mathbb E\,\operatorname{tr}(\Gamma_j\sigma_{X_m}) =\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\Pi\,\mathbb E[\Pi_{X_j}]\,\Pi\,\bar\sigma\bigr) =\operatorname{tr}\bigl((\Pi\,\mathbb E[\Pi_{X_j}]\,\Pi)(\Pi\bar\sigma\Pi)\bigr) \le D^{-1}\operatorname{tr}(\Pi\,\mathbb E[\Pi_{X_j}]\,\Pi) \le d/D.$$ The first equality factors the finite independent expectation into the product of its two means and distributes the finite trace sum using [F8]; the second uses [F7] and the support of the first factor. For the first inequality, $D^{-1}\Pi-\Pi\bar\sigma\Pi$ is nonnegative, so [F6] applied to its product with the nonnegative first factor gives the trace bound. For the last inequality, $I-\Pi$ is nonnegative and [F6]–[F7] give $\operatorname{tr}(\Pi\Pi_x\Pi)=\operatorname{tr}(\Pi_x\Pi)\le\operatorname{tr}(\Pi_x)\le d$. [F1, F6, F7, F8, given, algebra]

2.1 For the transmitted codeword $X_m$, [F3] applied with $S_0=\Gamma_m$ and $T_0=\sum_{j\ne m}\Gamma_j$ gives $$\operatorname{tr}((I-\Lambda_m)\sigma_{X_m})\le2\operatorname{tr}((I-\Gamma_m)\sigma_{X_m})+4\sum_{j\ne m}\operatorname{tr}(\Gamma_j\sigma_{X_m}).$$ The gentle bound [F2] for the global projection gives $\|\Pi\sigma_{X_m}\Pi-\sigma_{X_m}\|_1\le2\sqrt u$. Since $\|\Pi_{X_m}\|\le1$, trace-norm duality [F5] then gives $$\operatorname{tr}(\Gamma_m\sigma_{X_m}) =\operatorname{tr}(\Pi_{X_m}\Pi\sigma_{X_m}\Pi) \ge\operatorname{tr}(\Pi_{X_m}\sigma_{X_m})-2\sqrt u \ge1-u-2\sqrt u.$$ [F1, F2, F3, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Average step 2.1 over all messages and codebooks. Its first term is at most $2(u+2\sqrt u)$ by the acceptance estimate there, and each of the $M-1$ competing terms is at most $4d/D$ by step 1.2. Thus the expected average error has the claimed bound. Because the codebook sample space is finite, at least one realization has error no greater than its expectation. [step 2.1, step 1.2, algebra, choose] ∎"

      "item_id": "lem-it-cq-typical-projector-dimension",
      "status": "repair",
      "strategy": "direct",
      "proposed_proof": "**Given:** The finite states, ensemble, and $\delta>0$ from the Statement.

[F1] [[lem-finite-alphabet-iid-information-aep]]: for a finite IID law, the average surprisal converges in probability to its entropy, with an explicit variance-over-$n$ tail bound.

[F2] [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]]: $S(\rho)=-\sum_{\lambda_j>0}\lambda_j\ln\lambda_j$, with zero terms set to zero and units nats.

[F3] [[def-it-classical-quantum-state-and-holevo-information]]: $\bar\sigma=\sum_xp_x\sigma_x$ is the finite ensemble average state.

[F4] [[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]: each finite-dimensional density operator has an orthonormal eigenbasis with nonnegative eigenvalues.

[F5] [[thm-non-negative-operator-characterisations]]: a nonnegative operator with zero quadratic form at a vector annihilates that vector.

[F6] [[thm-chebyshev-inequality]] and [[def-variance-and-covariance]]: a finite random variable satisfies $\mathbb P(|Z-\mathbb EZ|\ge t)\le\operatorname{Var}(Z)/t^2$, and variance is the expected squared centered value.

[F7] [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]: $\ln(ab)=\ln a+\ln b$ for positive $a,b$.

[F8] [[prop-trace-is-linear]]: trace is linear over finite sums and scalar multiples.

[F9] [[lem-probability-measure-basic-identities]]: the probability of a finite union is at most the sum of its event probabilities.

[F10] [[def-qc-density-operator]]: every $\sigma_x$ and $\bar\sigma$ is nonnegative with trace one.





1.1 Diagonalize $\rho=\sum_{j:\lambda_j>0}\lambda_j|j\rangle\langle j|$ by [F4], and sample $J$ with law $\mathbb P(J=j)=\lambda_j$. The surprisal $-\ln\lambda_J$ is a finite-alphabet random variable of mean $S(\rho)$ by [F2]. For a product eigenvector with coordinates $j_1,\ldots,j_n$, its eigenvalue is $\prod_i\lambda_{j_i}$ and its surprisal is $-\ln(\prod_i\lambda_{j_i})=\sum_i-\ln\lambda_{j_i}$ by [F7]. Let $\Pi_n$ project onto product eigenvectors whose total surprisal lies in $[n(S(\rho)-\delta),n(S(\rho)+\delta)]$. The probability of this set tends to one by [F1]. Every selected product eigenvalue is at most $e^{-n(S(\rho)-\delta)}$ and at least $e^{-n(S(\rho)+\delta)}$; the first bound gives the operator inequality, and the second together with total mass at most one gives the rank bound. [F1, F2, F4, F7, given, construct, algebra]

1.2 For an input word $x^n$, let $N_x$ count its occurrences of $x$. Define $T_n$ by $N_x=0$ when $p_x=0$ and $|N_x/n-p_x|\le\kappa$ for every $p_x>0$. The coordinate indicators are independent under $p^{\otimes n}$ and have variance at most $1/4$; [F6]–[F9] give $p^{\otimes n}(T_n^c)\le|\mathcal X|/(4n\kappa^2)\to0$. For each $x$ with $p_x>0$, $\bar\sigma\succeq p_x\sigma_x$ by [F3] and [F10]; a vector in $\ker\bar\sigma$ therefore has zero quadratic form for $\sigma_x$, so [F5] gives $\operatorname{supp}\sigma_x\subseteq\operatorname{supp}\bar\sigma$. The spectral logarithm on the latter positive support is bounded in finite dimension by [F4], making $\mu_x:=\operatorname{tr}(\sigma_x[-\ln\bar\sigma])$ finite for every such $x$. Define this family only for $p_x>0$; the zero-probability symbols never occur in $T_n$. Choose $\kappa>0$ small enough that the empirical averages of each of the two finite families $S(\sigma_x)$ and $\mu_x$, restricted to $p_x>0$, differ from their $p$-averages by at most $\delta/2$ on $T_n$. These choices are possible because both restricted families are finite and their entries are finite. [F3, F4, F5, F6, F8, F9, F10, given, choose]

2.1 For each $x$, diagonalize $\sigma_x$ and, conditional on a fixed $x^n\in T_n$, measure each tensor factor in its chosen eigenbasis. The resulting surprisal variables $Z_i=-\ln\lambda_{J_i|x_i}$ are independent, finite, and uniformly bounded over the finite family of positive eigenvalues. By [F7], the product eigenvalue surprisal is their sum. Their means sum to $\sum_i S(\sigma_{x_i})$, which is within $n\delta/2$ of $nH(B|X)$ by step 1.2. Their sum has variance at most $nL^2$ for a fixed finite bound $L$; independence makes cross-covariances zero. Chebyshev [F6] shows that the probability of leaving the window $[n(H(B|X)-\delta),n(H(B|X)+\delta)]$ tends to zero uniformly over $x^n\in T_n$. Project onto the product eigenvectors whose surprisal lies in this window. Each selected eigenvalue is at most $e^{-n(H(B|X)-\delta)}$ and at least $e^{-n(H(B|X)+\delta)}$, proving conditional acceptance, the operator bound, and the rank bound as in step 1.1. [F2, F4, F6, F7, step 1.1, step 1.2, construct, algebra]

2.2 By [F10], $\bar\sigma$ is a state and $\bar\sigma-p_x\sigma_x=\sum_{z\ne x}p_z\sigma_z\succeq0$. Any $v\in\ker\bar\sigma$ has $\langle\sigma_xv,v\rangle=0$ when $p_x>0$, so [F5] gives $\sigma_xv=0$. Hence $\operatorname{supp}\sigma_x\subseteq\operatorname{supp}\bar\sigma$. On that support, the variable $-\ln\lambda_J$ obtained by measuring $\sigma_x$ in an eigenbasis of $\bar\sigma$ is finite and uniformly bounded over $x$ with $p_x>0$ and positive eigenvalue index. Its mean is $\mu_x$. The $p$-average of these means is $\operatorname{tr}(\bar\sigma[-\ln\bar\sigma])=S(\bar\sigma)$ by [F2], [F3], and [F8]. [F2, F3, F4, F5, F8, F10, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 For fixed $x^n\in T_n$, measuring the product state $\bigotimes_i\sigma_{x_i}$ in the product eigenbasis of $\bar\sigma^{\otimes n}$ gives independent surprisal variables with means $\mu_{x_i}$ and a common finite bound on their absolute values. By [F7], each product eigenvalue surprisal is the sum of the coordinate surprisals. Their means sum to within $n\delta/2$ of $nS(\bar\sigma)$ by step 1.2, and their sum has variance at most $nL'^2$ for a finite $L'$. Chebyshev [F6] therefore bounds uniformly by a quantity tending to zero the probability of leaving the $\delta$-window around $nS(\bar\sigma)$. The spectral projector of $\bar\sigma^{\otimes n}$ for that window accepts every such conditional product state with probability at least $1-u_n$. Its rank and compressed-operator bounds follow from its eigenvalue window exactly as in step 1.1. [F2, F4, F6, F7, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.2, construct, algebra]

4.1 Take $u_n$ to be the maximum of the uniform failure bounds in steps 2.1 and 3.1; both tend to zero, so $u_n\to0$. The global state acceptance follows from step 1.1 applied to $\bar\sigma$; all conditional and operator/rank assertions are those proved in steps 2.1 and 3.1. The constructions use only finite spectra, finite sums, and finite probability spaces, so no choice axiom is invoked. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎"

      "item_id": "thm-it-schumacher-quantum-source-coding",
      "status": "repair",

      "proposed_proof": "**Given:** A nonzero finite-dimensional source space, a density operator $\rho$, and the compression-code convention of the Statement.

[F1] [[def-it-quantum-source-and-compression-code]]: an $(n,M)$ code factors through an $M$-dimensional code space, and its squared entanglement fidelity is the overlap of a purification with the recovered state.

[F2] [[lem-it-cq-typical-projector-dimension]]: the spectral typical projector for $\rho^{\otimes n}$ has mass tending to one, rank at most $e^{n(S(\rho)+\delta)}$, and every included eigenvalue is at most $e^{-n(S(\rho)-\delta)}$.

[F3] [[lem-it-schmidt-rank-compression-fidelity-bound]]: any code factoring through dimension $M$ has entanglement fidelity at most the sum of the $M$ largest eigenvalues of $\rho$.

[F4] [[def-qc-quantum-channel]]: a quantum channel is completely positive and trace preserving.

[F5] [[thm-qc-kraus-choi-equivalence]] and [[thm-qc-trace-preserving-kraus-normalization]]: finite channels have finite Kraus families, and a trace-preserving family satisfies $\sum_jK_j^*K_j=I$.

[F6] [[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]: finite-dimensional states have finite spectral decompositions in orthonormal eigenbases.





1.1 Fix $\delta>0$, choose an ordered eigenbasis of $\rho$ once, and take the spectral typical projector $\Pi_n$ from [F2]. Order its finitely many product eigenvectors lexicographically; the resulting map to the first $r_n$ standard code basis vectors defines a partial isometry $W_n$ with $W_n^*W_n=\Pi_n$, where $r_n=\operatorname{rank}\Pi_n$. Let the code space have dimension $M_n=r_n+1$ and let $|\perp\rangle$ be its extra flag, orthogonal to $P_n:=W_nW_n^*$. Define $$\mathcal E_n(X)=W_nXW_n^*+\operatorname{tr}((I-\Pi_n)X)|\perp\rangle\langle\perp|,\qquad \mathcal D_n(Y)=W_n^*YW_n+\langle\perp|Y|\perp\rangle\,\rho^{\otimes n}.$$ The encoder Kraus family consists of $W_n$ and $|\perp\rangle\langle e_j|$ over an orthonormal basis of $\ker\Pi_n$; its Kraus squares sum to $\Pi_n+(I-\Pi_n)=I$. The decoder Kraus family consists of $W_n^*$ and $\sqrt{\lambda_j}|f_j\rangle\langle\perp|$ from a spectral decomposition $\rho^{\otimes n}=\sum_j\lambda_j|f_j\rangle\langle f_j|$; its Kraus squares sum to $P_n+|\perp\rangle\langle\perp|=I$. Thus both maps are channels by [F4]–[F6]. If $(K_\ell)_\ell$ is the finite composite Kraus family, substituting its action into [F1] gives $F_e^{(n)}=\sum_\ell|\langle\phi|(\operatorname{id}_R\otimes K_\ell)|\phi\rangle|^2$. The branch $K_0=W_n^*W_n=\Pi_n$ contributes $|\langle\phi|(\operatorname{id}_R\otimes\Pi_n)|\phi\rangle|^2=(\operatorname{tr}(\rho^{\otimes n}\Pi_n))^2$, and every other branch contributes a nonnegative squared modulus. Therefore $F_e^{(n)}\ge(\operatorname{tr}(\rho^{\otimes n}\Pi_n))^2\to1$. The basis order makes the sequence of codes explicit and uses no choice axiom. [F1, F2, F4, F5, F6, given, construct]

1.2 Suppose $\limsup_n n^{-1}\ln M_n<S(\rho)$. Choose $\delta>0$ and $N$ so that $M_n\le e^{n(S(\rho)-2\delta)}$ for $n\ge N$. Let $\Pi_n$ be the typical projector from [F2], and let $\epsilon_n=1-\operatorname{tr}(\rho^{\otimes n}\Pi_n)\to0$. Each eigenvalue in its range is at most $e^{-n(S(\rho)-\delta)}$. Therefore the sum of any $M_n$ eigenvalues of $\rho^{\otimes n}$ is at most $\epsilon_n+M_ne^{-n(S(\rho)-\delta)}\le\epsilon_n+e^{-n\delta}\to0$: the part outside the typical range contributes at most its total mass, and each selected eigenvalue inside contributes at most the displayed maximum. [F2, given, algebra, choose]

2.1 Since $r_n\le e^{n(S(\rho)+\delta)}$ and $e^{n(S+\delta)}\ge1$, $M_n=r_n+1\le2e^{n(S(\rho)+\delta)}$. Hence $\limsup_n n^{-1}\ln M_n\le S(\rho)+\delta$. Given $R>S(\rho)$, choose $\delta<R-S(\rho)$ to obtain the direct assertion. [F2, step 1.1, algebra, choose]

3.1 Apply [F3] to each $n$-block code with intermediate dimension $M_n$. Step 1.2 shows that its fidelity is at most a quantity tending to zero, hence $F_e^{(n)}\to0$. The argument includes zero eigenvalues and requires no full-rank source assumption. [F1, F3, step 1.2] ∎"

      "file": "items/thm-it-hsw-classical-quantum-channel-capacity.md",
      "item_id": "thm-it-hsw-classical-quantum-channel-capacity",
      "status": "repair",
      "strategy": "direct",
      "proposed_proof": "**Given:** A finite nonempty alphabet $\mathcal X$, nonzero finite-dimensional output space $H_B$, and one density operator $\rho_x$ for each input symbol.

[F1] [[def-it-cq-channel-block-code-and-error]]: codes use a uniform finite message, deterministic input words, a finite decoding POVM, average block error, and rate $n^{-1}\ln M$ nats/use.

[F2] [[def-it-classical-quantum-state-and-holevo-information]]: $\chi(\{p_x,\sigma_x\})=S(\sum_xp_x\sigma_x)-\sum_{p_x>0}p_xS(\sigma_x)$.

[F3] [[thm-it-holevo-measurement-bound]]: for any finite ensemble of states and any finite POVM, the classical mutual information of the input and the measurement outcome is at most the ensemble Holevo information.

[F4] [[lem-it-cq-typical-projector-dimension]]: for a finite ensemble, a high-probability input typical set has conditional and global output projectors with exponentially controlled rank and operator bounds, and uniform acceptance error tending to zero.

[F5] [[lem-it-square-root-cq-packing-bound]]: projectors satisfying those four bounds give expected average decoding error at most $2(u+2\sqrt u)+4(M-1)d/D$.

[F6] [[thm-it-finite-strong-subadditivity]]: for every finite tripartite state, $S(AB)+S(BC)\ge S(B)+S(ABC)$.

[F7] [[lem-it-finite-quantum-entropy-continuity]]: entropy is continuous in operator norm on finite-dimensional state spaces, including at zero eigenvalues.

[F8] [[thm-it-fano-inequality]]: for a finite message $M$ estimated from a finite observation with error probability $e$, $H(M\mid\widehat M)\le\ln2+e\ln|M|$.

[F9] [[thm-it-finite-entropy-chain-rule]]: for finite variables, $I(M;\widehat M)=H(M)-H(M\mid\widehat M)$.

[F10] [[def-qc-partial-trace]] and [[thm-qc-partial-trace-characterization-and-basis-independence]]: tracing tensor factors gives the usual marginals, is linear, and is independent of the chosen orthonormal basis.

[F11] [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]: the product basis is ordered factorwise and product operators act on their corresponding tensor factors.

[F12] [[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]: finite-dimensional Hermitian states have orthonormal eigenbases.

[F13] [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]: the natural logarithm is additive on finite products of positive numbers.

[F14] [[thm-heine-borel-rn]] and [[thm-extreme-value-metric]]: the closed probability simplex in finite-dimensional Euclidean space is compact, and a continuous real function on it attains a maximum.

[F15] [[def-operator-norm-on-a-finite-dimensional-inner-product-space]]: the operator norm is the maximum of $\|Av\|$ over unit vectors $v$.

[F16] [[def-qc-density-operator]]: each output state is nonnegative and has trace one.

[F17] [[thm-qc-partial-trace-characterization-and-basis-independence]] and [[prop-trace-is-linear]]: product-state marginals and finite mixture marginals are computed by partial trace and finite linearity.





1.1 Write $\chi_*=\sup_{p\in\Delta(\mathcal X)}\chi_p$. The simplex is nonempty, closed, and bounded. For each state $\rho_x$, [F12] diagonalizes it with nonnegative eigenvalues summing to one by [F16], so its action on a unit vector has norm at most one and [F15] gives $\|\rho_x\|\le1$. Therefore $\|\bar\rho_p-\bar\rho_q\|\le\sum_x|p_x-q_x|$. By [F7], the first entropy term in $\chi_p$ is continuous in $p$; the second is a finite linear sum. Thus [F14] shows the supremum is attained, so $\chi_*=\max_p\chi_p$. A point-mass input law gives $\chi_p=0$ by [F2], hence $\chi_*\ge0$. [F2, F7, F12, F14, F15, F16, given, algebra]

1.2 Fix $p$ and $0<R<\chi_p$. Choose $\delta>0$ with $R<\chi_p-2\delta$. Let $T_n$ be the input typical set from [F4], with excluded probability $\eta_n\to0$. Since $\eta_n\to0$, $p^{\otimes n}(T_n)=1-\eta_n>0$ for all sufficiently large $n$; for each earlier blocklength choose a fixed $x_0\in\mathcal X$ and use the one-message code with word $x_0^n$ and decoding POVM $\{I\}$. Draw each large-$n$ codeword independently from $p^{\otimes n}$ conditioned on $T_n$. Its mean output state is $$\bar\sigma_n'=\mathbb E[\rho_{X^n}\mid X^n\in T_n]\preceq(1-\eta_n)^{-1}\bar\rho_p^{\otimes n},\qquad \bar\rho_p=\sum_xp_x\rho_x.$$ The global typical projector from [F4] therefore obeys $\Pi_n\bar\sigma_n'\Pi_n\preceq(1-\eta_n)^{-1}e^{-n(S(\bar\rho_p)-\delta)}\Pi_n$. Each conditional projector has acceptance at least $1-u_n$, rank at most $e^{n(H(B|X)+\delta)}$, and the global projector accepts every conditioned codeword with at least $1-u_n$, where $u_n\to0$ and $H(B|X)=\sum_xp_xS(\rho_x)$. [F4, F12, given, algebra, choose]

1.3 Consider any $(n,M)$ code with $M\ge2$, uniform message $J$, output states $\omega_m=\bigotimes_i\rho_{x_i(m)}$, decoding outcome $\widehat J$, and average error $e$. The Holevo measurement bound [F3] gives $I(J;\widehat J)\le\chi(\{1/M,\omega_m\})$. Applying Fano [F8] and the finite mutual-information identity [F9], with $H(J)=\ln M$, yields $(1-e)\ln M\le\chi(\{1/M,\omega_m\})+\ln2$. For $M=1$, [F2] gives $\chi(\{1,\omega_1\})=S(\omega_1)-S(\omega_1)=0$, so the inequality is $0\le\ln2$. [F1, F2, F3, F8, F9, given, algebra, cases]

2.1 Set $M_n=\lfloor e^{nR}\rfloor$. The packing lemma [F5] with $d=e^{n(H(B|X)+\delta)}$ and $D^{-1}=(1-\eta_n)^{-1}e^{-n(S(\bar\rho_p)-\delta)}$ gives an expected average error bounded by $$2(u_n+2\sqrt{u_n})+4(M_n-1)(1-\eta_n)^{-1}e^{-n(\chi_p-2\delta)}.$$ Because $R<\chi_p-2\delta$, this tends to zero. The codebook space is finite; order $\mathcal X$ once and choose its lexicographically first codebook whose average error is at most this expectation. This defines a deterministic code for each $n$ without any choice axiom. [F1, F4, F5, step 1.2, algebra, construct, choose]

2.2 Let $p_i(x)=M^{-1}|\{m:x_i(m)=x\}|$ and $\bar\omega=M^{-1}\sum_m\omega_m$. By [F17], its $i$th marginal is $\bar\rho_i=\sum_xp_i(x)\rho_x$, which is a state by [F16]. For any bipartite state $\tau_{AC}$, tensor it with the unique state on a one-dimensional middle register $B=\mathbb C$: the four entropies in [F6] become $S(\tau_A),S(\tau_C),0,S(\tau_{AC})$, because tensoring with this factor leaves the spectrum unchanged. Thus [F6] implies $S(\tau_{AC})\le S(\tau_A)+S(\tau_C)$; iterating gives $S(\bar\omega)\le\sum_iS(\bar\rho_i)$. Product entropy is additive: diagonalize each $\rho_{x_i(m)}$ by [F12], so every positive product eigenvalue has logarithm equal to the sum of its coordinate logarithms by [F13]; zero eigenvalues contribute zero by [F2]. Summing these finite terms gives $S(\omega_m)=\sum_iS(\rho_{x_i(m)})$. Therefore $$\chi(\{1/M,\omega_m\})=S(\bar\omega)-\frac1M\sum_mS(\omega_m) \le\sum_{i=1}^n\left[S(\bar\rho_i)-\sum_xp_i(x)S(\rho_x)\right] =\sum_i\chi_{p_i}\le n\chi_*.$$ [F2, F6, F10, F11, F12, F13, F16, F17, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The selected codes have average error tending to zero and $n^{-1}\ln M_n\to R$. If $R=0$, the single-message code has zero error.
